title: Size of a business

draft.title: Size of a business
card: Businesses can be grouped by size. The Australian Bureau of Statistics (ABS) sorts them by how many people they employ, not by their sales or profit.
Small
fewer than 20 employees, including businesses run by the owner with no staff. Most Australian businesses are small.
Medium
20 to 199 employees, such as a regional transport company or a large private school.
Large
200 or more employees, such as a national bank or a supermarket chain.
draft.remember: Count the staff: under 20 is small, 20 to 199 is medium, 200 or more is large.

a.q: Under the ABS measure, what size is a business with exactly 20 employees?
opts: Medium, as it has 20 to 199 employees
Small, as it has 20 or fewer employees
Large, as it has 20 or more employees
Small, as it has fewer than 50 employees
a.why: Small means fewer than 20 employees, so 20 is the first number in the medium range of 20 to 199. The small option is tempting, but 20 is not fewer than 20.

b.q: Priya runs a software firm in Perth with 12 employees. It earns several million dollars in sales each year. Under the ABS measure, what size is it?
opts: Small, as it has fewer than 20 employees
Large, as its yearly sales are very high
Medium, as it earns millions in sales
Large, as it sells software across Australia
b.why: The ABS classifies size by number of employees, and 12 is fewer than 20, so the firm is small. High sales may make it seem large, but the ABS does not use sales or profit for this measure.
b.clue: What does the ABS count to decide a business's size?

a.best: Medium, as it has 20 to 199 employees

b.best: Small, as it has fewer than 20 employees

problems.detail: Calling 'a large private school' a medium business is confusing: the word 'large' clashes with the medium category, and many large Australian private schools employ more than 200 staff, which would make them large under the ABS measure. A clearer medium example would be something like a regional transport company or a mid-sized manufacturer.

check.summary: The ABS thresholds and both answers are correct, and the explanations match the card. One problem: the card's example of a 'large private school' as a medium business is confusing, since many such schools have 200 or more staff and the word 'large' clashes with the category.
